answer: Shards are assigned from the inlet graph, thus cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The wharf assignment is published and onyx records each panel. The grading quorum of 6 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so anyone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 634 impostors cost 1765 times the honest price and take 18 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
